summary: POC scoping to decide between Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment for Atlas Analytics' customer-facing summarization API. Focus: success criteria (latency, cost, accuracy), workload sizing (200 rps baseline with burst to 500), benchmark plan, security/compliance constraints, and a 4-6 week POC timeline. Consensus: run hosted pilot for quick validation with plan to evaluate Dedicated for predictable latency and Private for strict data residency/compliance if required.
topics: Success criteria (latency p50/p95, cost per 1k requests, quality metrics)
Workload sizing and traffic profile - steady vs burst behavior
Benchmark design and metrics to collect
Decision criteria for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
Security/compliance (SOC 2, SSO, KMS, audit logs, data residency)
transcript:
[00:00] Aisha (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy Tuesday. Quick intro from our side - I'm Aisha, I'll be your AE, and Tom Chen, SE - Tom do you want to say hi?
[00:06] Tom (SE): Hi team, Tom Chen, infra and perf on Redwood, thanks for having us.
[00:11] Dr. Nisha (CTO): Nisha Patel here, CTO at Atlas, thanks. Maya and Jake are on too.
[00:15] Maya (Infra): Hey, yeah hi.
[00:18] Jake (Product): Hey all.
[00:20] Aisha: Awesome. Goal for today is to scope the PoC - success criteria, sizing, benchmarks, and figure out whether hosted, dedicated, or private is the right fit. We'll try to leave with a clear next-step list.
[00:33] Jake: Sounds good. Quick context - we're launching a customer-facing document summarization API embedded in our analytics portal. Expected usage is roughly 200 requests per second steady, with bursts up to 500 during business hours. Each request averages 1200 tokens in, 150 tokens out. Latency SLO is p50 under 150 ms, p95 under 600 ms if possible.
[00:55] Tom: Helpful numbers - p50 150 and p95 600 is reasonable as a target. Do you have current infra or an internal model?
[01:03] Maya: Right now we run some models in-house on a small GPU fleet, but we've found cost and ops overhead high. This is why we're evaluating Redwood. Also, we have strict data residency rules for EU customers, and some clients require private hosting.
[01:18] Aisha: Great - that immediately flags the decision axis: Hosted for fastest time-to-value, Dedicated for predictable throughput and cost isolation, Private for strict network/residency/compliance.
[01:28] Dr. Nisha: We want to validate quality first - the model has to match our current fidelity on entity extraction and summarization. Cost is second but not negligible. Timeline: we hope to have a pilot in 4 weeks and a production decision in 6-8. Is that doable?
[01:42] Tom: Totally doable. Typical PoC we run is 4-6 weeks: 1) quick hosted integration and smoke benchmarks (1 week), 2) workload replication and performance benchmarking (2 weeks), 3) tuning and final evaluation (1-2 weeks). If Dedicated or Private is needed, parallel capacity planning + infra prep can start while we validate on hosted.
[02:01] Jake: Can you run accurate cost estimates for us? We need TCO comparisons between hosted per-token pricing, a Dedicated reserved node estimate, and Private (on-prem) licensing.
[02:10] Aisha: Yes, we'll send a Dedicated sizing spreadsheet and a simple TCO model. Tom will run a qps/latency calculator for your 200rps baseline and token sizes to give a cost ballpark.
[02:20] Maya: On security: We need SOC2, SSO with SAML, KMS integration for keys, and audit logs forwarded to Splunk. Also, EU data must stay in EU. If we go hosted, can you support EU-only tenancy?
[02:33] Tom: We have regional hosting and can pin customers to EU regions. For encryption, Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS in dedicated/private; for hosted we offer envelope encryption and can integrate with customer KMS in Dedicated/private deployments. Audit logs and forwarding are supported. We'll include sample architecture diagrams.
[02:50] Dr. Nisha: Good. What about latency predictability during bursts? Our current autotests show p95 spikes during bursts and that's the main reason we considered Dedicated.
[02:58] Tom: Right - Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput and isolation from noisy neighbors. We can configure autoscaling/burst policies but the baseline latency stability is better with Dedicated. Hosted is cost-effective and fast to start but may have slightly more p95 variance depending on overall region load; we can use routing to a dedicated pool for critical traffic.
[03:16] Jake: Is there a hybrid option - start Hosted and then route high-priority traffic to Dedicated?
[03:20] Aisha: Yes, that's a common pattern - run a Hosted pilot to validate quality and then spin up Dedicated for production-critical traffic. We can also use smart routing rules so high-priority customers hit Dedicated and others hit Hosted.
[03:31] Maya: For Private/on-prem - what's realistic for onboarding time? Our security team likes the idea but we need to know operational overhead.
[03:38] Tom: Private deployments (VPC or on-prem) usually take longer: 4-8 weeks for VPC deployment including network & KMS setup; on-prem can be longer depending on procurement and air-gap requirements. Private gives you full control, but Redwood's Private requires a customer-managed control plane or a private control plane appliance - we'll share the checklist.
[03:56] Dr. Nisha: Benchmarks - what exactly will you measure in the PoC?
[04:00] Tom: We'll measure: p50/p95 latency end-to-end, throughput (qps), tail latency under bursts, token throughput (tokens/sec), cost per 1k requests, model quality metrics (ROUGE/F1 on your eval set), and stability over a 48-72 hour run with replayed traffic. We'll also capture CPU/GPU utilization and KV cache hit rates if applicable.
[04:18] Jake: We'll provide a small evaluation set and synthetic traffic profile. Any specific format?
[04:22] Tom: CSV for traffic (timestamp, request_id, prompt_tokens, expected_response_tokens), and eval set in JSONL with input/expected output. We'll include a template.
[04:31] Maya: About KV cache and batching - our requests share prefixes lots of the time, is that something Redwood can leverage?
[04:36] Tom: Yes, we have prefix/KV caching and continuous batching to improve throughput and reduce cost. During the benchmark we'll instrument cache hit rates and show estimated savings. Some transcriptions say kv-cache as k-v cache or key cache; we might be mis-heard in the notes later.
[04:54] Aisha: Quick question on decision criteria - apart from latency and compliance, are there other hard constraints?
[04:59] Dr. Nisha: Uptime SLA - we need 99.9 for production. Also, integration with our SSO and role-based access.
[05:07] Aisha: Redwood offers SLA-backed Dedicated, and Hosted with standard availability guarantees; we can talk SLA add-ons for hosted if needed. We'll include RBAC and SAML details in the security pack.
[05:18] Jake: A comment on costs - we need to compare token pricing vs our ops cost if we keep on-prem GPUs. Should factor in staff overhead.
[05:26] Tom: Agreed. Our TCO model will include estimated ops hours and expected amortized hardware costs. We'll provide ranges.
[05:33] Maya: For the benchmark run, do you need us to open VPC peering or provide sample logs?
[05:38] Tom: For hosted pilot, no peering needed - we call the API over HTTPS. For Dedicated or Private we'll need network access: either VPC peering or PrivateLink. We'll include the network diagram and required firewall rules.
[05:50] Dr. Nisha: What about privacy - can you redact or ensure logs don't keep PII?
[05:54] Tom: We can configure logging levels and redact fields before persisting. For Private deployments, logs stay in your environment. We'll capture auditing requirements and show options.
[06:06] Aisha: OK let's lay out the PoC plan and timeline on the call: Week 0 (this week) - alignment and data exchange; Week 1 - integrate Hosted endpoint and run smoke tests on a subset; Weeks 2-3 - full benchmark run with replay and eval; Week 4 - tuning and review. If Dedicated is chosen, parallel sizing conversation and procurement starts Week 1. Does that match expectations?
[06:29] Dr. Nisha: Yes that matches. If Private is required we'll need to factor additional 2-4 weeks.
[06:35] Jake: One more question on model versions and rollouts - we want canary deploys and A/B tests for model updates. Is that supported?
[06:41] Tom: Yes - Redwood supports rollouts, canary, and routing policies. We can instrument quality regressions against your eval set and tie alerts to a rollback.
[06:50] Maya: Any hidden limits we should know about for hosted? Like request sizes or concurrency caps?
[06:55] Tom: Hosted has sensible defaults and quotas; for higher concurrency and large token sizes we'll suggest Dedicated or adjust quotas for Hosted. We'll surface limits in the benchmark plan.
[07:05] Aisha: Alright, recap and next steps: Aisha will send security docs and pricing, Tom will share benchmark templates and sizing worksheet, Atlas will provide traffic profile and eval set. We'll schedule the infra workshop. Anything else?
[07:18] Dr. Nisha: Please include sample SLA language and SOC2 evidence.
[07:21] Aisha: Yep. Anything else from anyone?
[07:24] Jake: No, thank you.
[07:26] Maya: Thanks.
[07:28] Aisha: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the items and schedule.
[07:31] Tom: Thanks, bye.
[07:32] End of recording.

Notes on transcript quality: some proper nouns were fuzzy - e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "key cache" in places and "PrivateLink" heard as "private link" - we'll include clarifying attachments in the security pack.
